title: louis-agent · the C# AI agent framework
text: The C# AI agent framework Build agents, not infrastructure. louis-agent runs the loop, guards every tool call, measures every request and puts your agent in front of people. The engine runs its loop, an identity says who it is, and a pack says what it can do. Your program names the identities and packs it wants, then starts a host that puts the agent in front of people. This is the line that starts the coding agent, from its real program. Program.cs Ask Copy await CliHost.RunAsync(args, CodingCatalog.Create(), new HostServices(WebAccess.Create, OtlpTelemetry.Instance, Providers: [AnthropicProvider.Instance, OllamaProvider.Instance, OpenAiCompatibleProvider.Instance])); Engine, identities and packs The architecture The whole framework Every project, in its family. The framework's projects sit in five families, a folder each. The engine runs the agent, and the hosts put it in front of people. The web is what every website is built on. The evals measure an agent, and the tools draw the docs' pictures and read what a model was really billed. Beside the five families sit the things built with them. They show where a project of your own would go, and each one is real code you can open and run. Puls, an assistant built on the framework's packages, lives in a repository of its own. packs/tools The ready-made packs, from files and git to the web, the docs and a calculator. Their tests and web views sit beside them in folders of their own, so you can take the tools alone. src/site The framework's own websites. louis-agent.dev with the guide in its corner, this site with Orbi beside it, and the showroom's three made-up businesses. demos/louis-agent The coding agent and the triage team, with the code-review web app and the programs that start them. demos/starter The smallest site there is, and the template that dotnet new louis-site makes a new one from. The public site Puls, in its own repository Spawn a site Why C# One language, end to end. The engine, the hosts, the tools and the tests are all C#. The websites are Blazor, so C# runs in the browser too. Underneath is Microsoft.Extensions.AI, one chat client for Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and Ollama, and the engine runs its own loop over it. Our own loop Where providers differ Your own hardware It runs where you put it. Run it in Docker on your own machine or server, with no cloud agent service in between. Point it at a local model through Ollama, and the model runs on that machine too. Set it up
